report:
Based on the evidence gathered, your suspicion is well supported.

## Conclusion: The evidence does not support ginkgo biloba as an effective tinnitus treatment

The most authoritative source, the **Cochrane systematic review** (updated evidence synthesis of high-quality randomized controlled trials, including one large study with 1,543 participants), concluded there is **no reliable evidence that ginkgo reduces tinnitus severity compared to placebo** (cochrane.org/hr/evidence/CD003852_ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus).

This aligns with earlier rigorous trials. A landmark double-blind, placebo-controlled study published in *BMJ* found that **Ginkgo biloba extract LI 1370 had no greater therapeutic effect than placebo** for tinnitus, nor for other symptoms of "cerebral insufficiency" (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC26593/). Similarly, Rejali et al. conducted a randomized double-blind trial plus a meta-analysis of prior randomized trials and concluded that **"Ginkgo biloba does not benefit patients with tinnitus"** (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8564151_Ginkgo_biloba_does_not_benefit_patients_with_tinnitus_A_randomized_placebo-controlled_double-blind_trial_and_meta-analysis_of_randomized_trials).

It's worth noting the evidence base is mixed and contested: some smaller/older systematic reviews and industry-linked studies (particularly those using the specific standardized extract EGb 761®) reported statistically significant benefits in a handful of trials (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.2147/NDT.S22793). However, these positive findings have not held up under the stricter methodological scrutiny of Cochrane's meta-analysis, which is generally considered the gold standard for evaluating clinical evidence, and larger, independent trials have consistently failed to replicate benefit over placebo.

**Bottom line:** The highest-quality, most independent evidence (Cochrane review and large RCTs) indicates ginkgo does not meaningfully relieve tinnitus symptoms, despite some conflicting smaller studies—many tied to the extract's manufacturer.
